### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **32** documentable anchor(s).

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `current_user (literal, 34 pages)`
- **14** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `19788a62198f4282e4de4a7233b01edcdea9d39c` — the merge of head `e99141ce2af26323c48c69eff359b5d45b3da706` into base `1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 19788a62198f4282e4de4a7233b01edcdea9d39c && git checkout 19788a62198f4282e4de4a7233b01edcdea9d39c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04 e99141ce2af26323c48c69eff359b5d45b3da706 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04 && git merge --no-ff e99141ce2af26323c48c69eff359b5d45b3da706

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e99141ce2af26323c48c69eff359b5d45b3da706`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #22565 (body and all 13 comments — rulings A′ `6094431558` and S `6094850599`, the seat orders, the three dev reports, the ACCEPTs `6094065925` and `6095657891`), card #22636 (body), PR #22609 (body, its 8-file list, the net diff against merge-base `1b99388505`: +1276 / −6), and the engine, executor and spec sources at this head, read only. Check-runs on the head: 42 across 17 suites — 37 success, 5 skipped by path or opt-in filters (Auto Label, Build Docs, Check PR Size, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke), 0 failure, 0 still running. Green among them: Lint & Repo Gates (the job that runs `check:migration-registry`, `check:adr-0087-registration`, `check:changeset-no-major`, `check:empty-changeset`), Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Test Core 1–6, every Type Check job, Dogfood Regression Gate 1–3, Temporal Conformance.

### ① Derived judgments

**The refused set — right.** Every root the judge refuses is one the run leaves unbound, measured against `seedRunVariables`, `seedDeclaredVariables` and `celScope` in `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts`: a run binds the declared variables (`isInput` from `params`, else `defaultValue`), `$record` and `record` plus the record's keys flattened under a has-guard, `previous` (`null` when absent), `$runId` / `$flowName` / `$flowLabel`; `celScope` then adds `vars` and `current_user` after the spread. `params` is never spread, so a bare param key is unbound. The judge's `ENGINE_BOUND_ROOTS` (`record`, `previous`, `vars`, `current_user`) is exactly the non-`$` engine set; a `$` name has no CEL spelling and stays the text-slot rule's. `buildScope` in `@objectstack/formula` mounts `user`, `ctx.user` and `os.user` only from `ctx.currentUser`, and `celScope` hands it `extra` and `record` alone, so `user`, `ctx` and `os` are unbound in every flow CEL site — refused with the `current_user` remedy, while `os.env` and the like get the general refusal (pinned). The flow's own bindings come from `collectFlowVariableNames`, composed not copied, and match the executors: `outputVariable` (`crud-nodes.ts`, `screen-nodes.ts`, `subflow-node.ts`, `map-node.ts`), `iteratorVariable` / `indexVariable` (`loop-node.ts`, `map-node.ts`), `errorVariable` (`try-catch-node.ts`, default `$error`), assignment keys in all three shapes (`logic-nodes.ts`), node outputs under the node id; plus the two that reader does not collect — screen field names (`applyResumeSignal` lands `signal.variables` under plain names) and `loop`'s schema default `item`. Record fields: every declared object's fields with injected columns, because the run flattens whichever `context.record` its entrance hands it. Comprehension macros and `cel.bind` are scoped as cel-js scopes them; CEL's own names are excluded through `firstUndeclaredReference`. No root a valid judged flow reads is refused.

**The node-level stand-downs — right.** `script` and `connector_action` get the live variable map; `wait`, `subflow` and `map` declare `resumeAuthority: 'any'`, and `applyResumeSignal` folds any plain-named bag; a screen with no field contract (`refuseInvalidScreenInput` checks a bag only against declared fields); every type outside the measured closed set. `approval` / `approval_revise` are closed by `resumeAuthority: 'service'` (declared in `domains/automation.ts`) and their service-built signal lands outputs under the node id — I found no plain-name `variables` write in those declarers — so keeping them in the closed set is right.

**A′ — every entrance the stack declares that can hand a flow a record of an undeclared object opens it, and nothing else does — right.** I enumerated every caller of the engine's `execute` at this head. (1) A record trigger: start `config.objectName`. (2) The time-relative sweep: `config.timeRelative.object` — `time-relative-trigger.ts` hands each matched row as `record` (and as `params`). (3) The inbound hook: `api-trigger.ts` hands the body as `record` and `params`, armed only where `resolveFlowTriggerKind` answers `api` — the same resolver the engine binds with (`engine.ts:3721`), so a `type: 'api'` flow that also carries a `schedule` resolves `schedule` at both ends and is consistently not opened. (4) A stack action: `dispatchFlowAction` hands `subject.record` and omits `object` for an object-less key, and it is reached only through a registered action (`domains/actions.ts:512` reads `declaration.action`; `invokeBusinessAction` goes through `resolveActionByName`), so a page's inline `actionType: 'flow'` button is no record entrance, and `id` is the most an object-less launch binds. (5) A `map` node: `map-node.ts:177-183` sets `record: item` only for an item with a string `id`, with `itemObject` falling back to the parent's `context.object`, so an absent `itemObject` is rightly read as unknowable. (6) An open `subflow` / `map` parent: both executors spread the parent's context (record included), never its variables, so a child needs exactly the parent's record keys, and the fixpoint carries exactly that. Not entrances: the REST trigger routes and the declarative endpoint build `buildAutomationContext` (`automation.ts:107-135`, `endpoint-executor.ts:572`), which emits `params`, `recordId`, `object`, `event` and no `record`; the engine never hydrates from `object` + `recordId`; a schedule run hands none; MCP `run_action` is the action entrance; no hook, agent or component schema names a flow with a record (`endpoint.zod.ts`'s `target` rides the no-record door). The schema keys the reader cites exist as cited: `ActionSchema` `type: 'flow'` / `target` / `objectName`, `objects[].actions` and `stack.actions` both `z.array(ActionSchema)` (and `recordsOf` reads the keyed form too), `MapConfigSchema.flowName` / `.itemObject`, `SubflowConfigSchema.flowName`, `TimeRelativeTriggerSchema.object`.

**S — only this judgment stands down at the runtime publish gate — right.** `runtime-gate.ts:1102` passes `runtimeWriteType: args.type` on every runtime write; inside `runStackExpressionPasses` the new `runtimeGateWrite` is read in exactly two places — the entrance index is left empty, and `flowCelRootScope` receives `perWriteSnapshotEntrance()`, so `unboundFlowCelRoots` answers `[]` and the near-miss withdrawal never runs. Nothing else in the flow pass branches on it; `checkDeclaredValue`'s new `{ refused }` return changes no side effect. The stand-down keys on any runtime write rather than on a flow write by name, but only a flow write's snapshot carries `flows` (`CONTEXT_STACK_KEYS` is objects, permissions, books, datasets), so the two are the same set. The gate pin shows the brace-trap verdict still refusing on edge `e2` while `e1`'s `user.id` is not refused there, and the build door refusing the same root on the same flow. Nothing of W rides: no `metadata-protocol` or `runtime-gate.ts` path in the file list. Not A: no `service-automation` path, `celScope` untouched.

**The D3 entry and `registry.ts` — right.** `18.flow-cel-unbound-root-refused.ts` follows the `18.{id}.ts` convention; its `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria` and leading comment are identical to the regenerated `semantic:18` region in the diff; the generator orders entries by major then id, and `check:migration-registry` is green in Lint & Repo Gates. The `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment sits in id order between `flow-binding-variable-dollar-name-refused` and `flow-decision-edge-branching-first-match`, as the step-18 rationale test requires. Its `order: 92` is the third fragment at that order — two already sit there at the merge-base — and the composer sorts by order then id (`registry.ts:5006`), so the join is deterministic and that test asserts no uniqueness. Noted, not a defect.

**Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, named:** (a) `objectstack validate` refuses an unbound root at each flow CEL site it visits — the narrowing, right; (b) the flattened-scope near-miss warning is withdrawn where the refusal names the same root — one finding per root, pinned, right; (c) a near-miss of a trigger field on a judged flow moves from warning to error — the same narrowing, stated in the body's severity note, right; (d) six fixtures across `lint-flow-patterns.test.ts` and `validate-expressions.test.ts` now declare the names they read — fixtures only, no accept-set change; (e) `@objectstack/lint`'s public shape is unchanged (`flow-cel-root-scope.ts` is not re-exported from `index.ts`); its behaviour narrows. No widening anywhere.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/22565-flow-cel-unbound-root-refused.md` names `@objectstack/lint: major` and `@objectstack/spec: major` — the two packages the diff publishes in; no other package changes. AGENTS.md: `(narrowing)` is BREAKING; `.changeset/pre.json` is `mode: pre`, tag `next`, which is what `check:changeset-no-major` admits (green). The PR body's third line and the changeset both carry `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — right: `objectstack validate` accepts strictly less and nothing is widened. The body carries the single ADR-0087 marker `registered flow-cel-unbound-root-refused`, the FROM → TO table, the one-line fix and the measured reach (67 flows, 0 refusals, 1 opened by the inbound hook); `check:adr-0087-registration` and `check:empty-changeset` are green in the same job. Spec publishes something new (the D3 record) and owes its own entry — it has one, in the same file. `skip-changeset` would be wrong here and is not used.

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

### ③ Boundary flags

- Round-1 open question (bound set A / A′ / B / C): answered A′ by triage `6094431558`; this head implements A′ as ruled (above). Closed.
- Round-2 open question (runtime door S / W / K / B): answered S by triage `6094850599`; W is #22636, filed `pm:blocked`, ordered after #22609, and its done-when removes this PR's stand-down. Closed.
- Round-1 deviation 1 (record keys of every stack object): superseded by A′, which pairs the widening with the entrance stand-downs. Closed.
- Round-1 deviation 2 (`lint-flow-patterns.test.ts`, pass 3's surface, +5 fixture lines): in the diff as stated and textually disjoint from pass 3; the seat accepted it and told #19939. Closed.
- Round-1 deviation 3 (projections not regenerated): no `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` or `spec-changes.json` in the file list; `check:upgrade-guide` and `check:spec-changes` green. Closed.
- Round-1 deviation 4 (engine roots as a local constant): verified against `celScope`; it is not a `$`-name list. Closed.
- Round-3 deviation 1 (one lock acquisition held 909s): process, no finding. Closed.
- **Round-3 deviation 2, put to this review — a `map` child of an open parent has no pin of its own. Is a pin owed? Yes, owed; not blocking.** The behaviour is right: `map-node.ts` spreads the parent context and sets `record` only for an id-bearing item, so a non-id item leaves the child holding the parent's record, and the fixpoint must open it. The code path is the subflow edge's own kind-agnostic loop, so this head cannot be wrong where the pinned subflow case is green; what the missing pin leaves unguarded is a later kind-specific refactor (a map child with a declared `itemObject` taken to need no inheritance), which the executor shows would be wrong. Carrier: #22636, whose closing criterion is A′ at both doors with the same pins — the map-edge pin belongs in that set; the seat may land it sooner as a test-only follow-up. An acceptance note, not a condition of this verdict.
- Round-3 deviation 3 (`platform-objects` reach from a source scan): it declares no flows. Closed.
- Round-3 deviation 4 (the start-object check moved into the entrance reader): verdict unchanged and pinned (`a record trigger: an undeclared start config.objectName stands down`). Closed.
- Round-3 deviation 5 (worktree and clone cleanup): hygiene. Closed.
- Out-of-scope finding 1 (`has()` hint faults on an unbound variable): carried to #19939 pass 3 by the seat. Findings 2 and 3 (projection drift until #22485; the hand-measured closed node set and engine roots): acceptance notes with no carrier — I concur; the second is the drift a `service-automation` parity pin would close, and it needs a lint dev-dependency there, so a card of its own if anyone wants it.
- Open questions at this head: none. Escalations: none.
